subject: AWS Marketplace listing: SLA footnotes, procurement snippets & pricing parity review
messages:
From: Maria Perez <maria.perez@amazon.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procure@acme-analytics.com>; LegalOps <legal@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed SLA footnotes & procurement snippets for Acme listing

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the quick sync this morning. As discussed, attaching two starter artifacts the Acme procurement team asked for: a short set of "SLA footnotes" they can include in their internal procurement packet, and a one-page procurement snippet the field can hand to legal (attachments: aws-sla-footnotes-v1.docx, procurement-snippets-acme.pdf).

Two items we flagged that would accelerate listing approval on the AWS side:
- A clear, plain-language footnote for downtime measurement and credits (example in doc).
- Confirmation on pricing parity / private offer handling — Acme wants to ensure they can procure via Private Offers at the same SKU pricing as public listing (they specifically called out predictable billing start-date and invoice contact).

If you can confirm whether Redwood is comfortable with: (a) the proposed credit calculation language, and (b) a parity statement for private offers, I can start routing to the marketplace review queue today.

Link to the AWS seller console checklist: https://seller.amazon.com/marketplace-checklist

Thanks,
Maria
---
Maria Perez
AWS Marketplace Program Manager
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Maria Perez <maria.perez@amazon.com>, Acme Procurement <procure@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Sep 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed SLA footnotes & procurement snippets for Acme listing

Maria —

Appreciate the packet. Attaching to our legal/ops queue. Kimberly and Laura: please review the two attachments and propose redlines for the public listing footnote and the Acme procurement snippet. High-level asks from our side:

- We should avoid committing to guarantee parity that forces us to match any promotional discounts — parity should be "SKU base price parity for the same SKU and term; promotions excluded" (suggested wording below).
- Verify the credit calculation doesn't create an open-ended liability for longer tail incidents. We can accept a simple per-incident credit formula tied to percent uptime per billing month.
- Confirm whether we can include a short operational contact for invoice/start-date confirmation in the procurement snippet (Acme asked explicitly for a named billing contact).

Kimberly — could you draft two short bullets for the marketplace product page: one SLA footnote (1-2 lines) and one procurement-note (1-3 bullets) that the field can paste into the Acme PO packet? Laura, please flag any legal redlines you see.

HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.company/deal/DEAL-ACME-2028-09 (added notes).

Thanks — I can loop in Sales Ops for the private offer flow after legal sign-off.

–Aditya

Date: Wed, 19 Sep 2028 08:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed SLA footnotes & procurement snippets for Acme listing

Aditya — quick pass from product/ops on the two artifacts. Edits inline below and I uploaded a single consolidated doc to Drive (https://drive.google.com/open?id=1abcSLA-Notes).

Suggested marketplace footnote (1 line, fits listing):
"Monthly uptime excludes scheduled maintenance; remedial credits, when applicable, are calculated as a percentage of the monthly invoice and apply to the next billing cycle."

Procurement snippet (1 page summary for Acme PO packet):
- Billing effective date: charges begin on service activation date confirmed by the named billing contact.
- Private Offer parity: Redwood will extend the public SKU base price to Private Offers for the same SKU and term. Promotional discounts or third-party reseller pricing are excluded.
- Incident credits: credits per incident capped at 50% of that month’s invoice; cumulative credits capped at 100% per 12-month period.

Notes:
- The parity line is intentionally narrow — we call out "base price for same SKU and term" to avoid matching time-limited promos.
- We should not include data-residency guarantees in the listing footnote (says more in the procurement doc if customer needs it).

I'll let Legal take the redlines on the credit caps/wording. If that looks OK, I think we can give Maria the green light to push to AWS review.

Kimberly
Product Ops | Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Maria Perez <maria.perez@amazon.com>, Acme Procurement <procure@acme-analytics.com>, LegalOps <legal@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Sep 2028 14:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed SLA footnotes & procurement snippets for Acme listing

Thanks team — legal looked through Kimberly’s suggested language and we have one small redline to keep the credit mechanics clear for accounting: replace "credits per incident capped at 50% of that month’s invoice" with "for any qualifying incident, remedial credit will be calculated as 50% of the prorated affected service fees for that billing month, not to exceed 50% of that month’s invoice." This keeps the intent but ties credits back to prorated fees.

On Private Offers: approved to include the parity sentence Kimberly proposed, provided we add this parenthetical: "(excludes one-off promotional discounts and third-party reseller offers)."

Action items / next steps:
- Aditya: confirm billing contact name and email for the procurement snippet (Acme asked to list a contact).
- Sean / Sales Ops: after Aditya confirms, prepare Private Offer template and routing (DocuSign link for PO to follow).
- Maria: once you have the final text we’ll sign off formally.

Docs attached: procurement-snippets-acme.pdf (annotated)

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
